question: Does retaining the last explicit gripper target during subsequent arm movements reduce slip and improve task execution?
rationale: Stage35 true-state logs show transient lift/slip. Frozen approach uses each measured gripper opening as its next action. Released Motion holds self.grip commands; distinguish persistent command from measured opening. 81 goal probes show limited target-pose recovery; no goal changes in this experiment.
treatment: At each issued action retain the last explicitly commanded gripper target independently for each arm until the next gripper command. Before any command leave measured-state behavior unchanged. Observed/provided state remains measured.
endpoints: held object displacement around lift and transport
returned after planner failure or budget
limits: Manual compatibility-interface correction, not autonomous System2 generation
All five layouts previously exposed; exploratory mechanism evidence, not generalization
Persistent command alone cannot solve infeasible transport poses
New side logging in both conditions; no cross-stage speed claims
Fresh controls; historical stage35 cases are not counted again
